Phase 7 of #34, over the same ingestion chain the cron uses. Slices are
independent, so one bad slice costs one retry rather than a restart; and a
retried step reads what the previous attempt stored in R2 rather than
re-fetching, because the platform re-runs a whole step and every fetch inside

Phase 7 of #34, over the same ingestion chain the cron uses. Slices are
independent, so one bad slice costs one retry rather than a restart; and a
retried step reads what the previous attempt stored in R2 rather than
re-fetching, because the platform re-runs a whole step and every fetch inside
one is a request to somebody else's server.

Slices run oldest first, and a document whose key carries no date belongs to no
window. The slice size stays an unchecked bet against Cloudflare's Workflow
limits and says so in its own name.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.

Phase 6 of #34. Pure functions over a series — no store, no model — so a case
can plant a step change or an outlier and assert exactly what comes back.

both ends dated there is no interval and nothing is recorded.

prevent, sitting in the fixtures.

one that drifts without stepping must all come back empty.

input.body:
**Resolved. The repository was made public, and Actions started working in the same hour.**

The boundary is clean enough to be a diagnosis rather than a guess. Nothing in the repository changed between these two runs — same head sha, same workflow file, same cron:

| run | when | result |
|---|---|---|
| Claudinite scheduler #46 | 2026-08-23T10:01:49Z | failure, 5s, no logs |
| Claudinite scheduler #47 | 2026-08-23T11:01:32Z | **success** |

Run #47 fired on its own schedule before anything was dispatched by hand. The only change in that hour was visibility, and public repositories run on free minutes — which is what this issue guessed at from the other side (Actions disabled, a spending limit, or exhausted included minutes) and could not confirm from inside a session.

Outage window: **2026-08-22T00:01Z → 2026-08-23T~10:30Z**, about 34½ hours, every run in the repository, across workflows no merge touched.

**Everything the backlog was waiting on has now run green.**

| run | what it verifies |
|---|---|
| [product #33](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635407554) on `fae2229` | all fifteen unverified merges at once — 62 default · 13 server · 14 screen · dry-run resolving three bindings · `ship main` correctly no-opping with no account |
| [product #35](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635616096) on #66 | the same, on a `pull_request` trigger |
| [CI #41](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635616100) | both Claudinite conformance sweeps |
| [product #36](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635670688) on `9abb631` | `main` after the merge |
| [preflight #1](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635678175) | the provisioning checklist, reporting what #27 still needs |

Counts read off the CI logs rather than carried over from the local runs: **62 / 13 / 14**, matching what every one of those fifteen squash messages claimed. The bisect list did not need to be bisected.

One thing the first green run surfaced immediately: every job warned that its actions still target Node 20. Fixed in #66, verified by the absence of the warning in the runs after it.

The scheduler's queue is live again too — #47 was a real scheduler run, so the `task:blocked` work items are back on their own cadence.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.

The only change in that hour was visibility. Public repos run on free minutes, which is exactly what [#39](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/39) guessed at and couldn't confirm from inside a session. Outage window: 2026-08-22T00:01Z → ~10:30Z today, about 34½ hours. **[#39 is closed.](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/39#issuecomment-5385682959)** **All fifteen unverified merges are verified in one run.** [product #33 on `fae2229`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635407554) — 62 default, 13 server, 14 screen, the dry-run resolving three bindings, and `ship main` correctly no-opping with no account. I read those counts off the CI logs rather than carrying them over; they match what every one of the fifteen squash messages claimed. The bisect list never had to be bisected. **The first green run immediately found something**, which is the argument for running CI rather than reasoning about it. Every job warned that `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4` target Node 20 and are being *forced* onto Node 24 — a deadline, not noise. [PR #66](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/66) fixes it ([#65](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/65), merged `9abb631`). The reason that took reading rather than guessing: | | v4 | v5 | v6 | |---|---|---|---| | `checkout` | node20 | **node24** | node24 | | `setup-node` | node20 | **node24** | node24 | | `upload-artifact` | node20 | node20 | **node24** | `upload-artifact@v5` is *still Node 20*. "Bump everything to v5" would have left the warning on the one step that only runs when a screen golden has already failed. Each is read from that action's own `action.yml` at the tag. The odd version has its reason on the line, because the next person's instinct will be to make it match its neighbours.
**`.github/workflows/`** — `product.yml`, `preflight.yml` and `claudinite-ci.yml` move to `checkout@v5`/`setup-node@v5`, and `upload-artifact` to v6. The two vendored Claudinite workflows are untouched.
Three things worth knowing: **A gap I can't close from here.** The vendored scheduler and executor are already on v5, but their three `actions/github-script@v7` steps are Node 20 (`@v8` is the Node 24 one). That belongs in Claudinite, not here — noted in #65. **Preflight ran and exited red.** Not a break: [it reported the whole checklist correctly](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32635678175) and named #27. "Not ready to deploy" is its verdict, and exit 1 is how it says so. **The repo is public now, so I checked what that opens.** No `pull_request_target` anywhere. Fork PRs can run `product.yml` and `claudinite-ci.yml` with read-only tokens and no secrets — the deploy job is gated off for `pull_request`. The executor fires on `issues: [labeled]`, and labelling needs write access, so a stranger opening an issue can't wake agent work. And every figure, quote and publisher in the repo is still invented, which is the state I'd want it in on the day it became readable by anyone. > ⚠️ Still open: [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27) Cloudflare provisioning — now the only thing between `main` and a deployed site, and it blocks #34 phases 0/1/5, the stance model, and #36's rollback · [#32](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/32) source recon needs your green light · [#33](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/33) what names a cluster · **the real roster** · one gap for the Claudinite canon (`github-script@v7`)

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

content.text: I've read the harness and the standing promises before designing anything. Two decisions are genuinely yours, and they change what gets built.

questions.question: Most of what you listed doesn't exist yet — the API has no analytics, no error sink, no search or share counters. Corpus counts and crawl state I can build from what the server already knows. But "most-searched personas", "most shared conflicts" and client errors mean collecting data about the people using the site, and client error reporting needs a POST endpoint — which breaks `5.8` ("a write method is rejected with 405") and the design's "no write surface". What should the dashboard be allowed to collect?

options.label: Corpus + operations only (Recommended)
options.description: Entity counts, statement distribution, crawl state, server-side errors. Nothing about visitors. No write surface, no privacy promise changes, and it's fully buildable now — a product whose roster note says "we do not track personal activity" logging what its readers search for is a tension worth avoiding unless you want it.

options.label: Add aggregate counters, no queries
options.description: Per-page and per-figure view counts, kept as totals with no query strings, no IPs, no identities. Answers "which personas get looked at" without recording what anyone typed. Still needs a write path and a disclosure line, but the thing retained is a number.

options.label: Everything you listed, including search terms
options.description: Log search queries and share events verbatim so "most-searched" and "most-shared" are exact. Most useful, and the largest change: a new write surface, retained free-text a visitor typed, and a privacy disclosure that has to be written before the code.

questions.question: You said GitHub Pages and "using the user credentials". A static Pages site cannot hold a secret — anything it ships is public. Which way should the dashboard get its data?

options.label: Token pasted into the dashboard (Recommended)
options.description: Pages serves the dashboard; you paste an admin token once and the browser keeps it locally, sending it to a protected /api/v1/admin route. No secret in the repo or the built page, corpus counts still render without one, and it's the only option where the dashboard is live rather than a snapshot.

options.label: Public status endpoint, public dashboard
options.description: No credentials anywhere: the Worker serves the numbers openly and the page renders them. Simplest by far and arguably fine for corpus counts — but error messages leak internals, and on a public repo the dashboard is world-readable.

options.label: CI builds a snapshot into Pages
options.description: A scheduled Action holds the Cloudflare token in repo secrets, fetches state — including Cloudflare's own Worker analytics, which gives request counts and error rates with no instrumentation — and commits static JSON. Credential never ships; data is as fresh as the last run, and public once committed.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. ## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- map-a-data-source: Reconnaissance on a website you want data from but don't control — locate the real data surface (hydration blob, client API, or markup) and write the findings down before any parser exists. Use when adding a new source to a scraper, or when an existing source stops parsing and you suspect the site changed shape.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). input.title: An operator dashboard: what the corpus holds and what the crawl did
input.body:
There is no way to look at the running product and see what it holds or what it last did. The public API answers questions about *one* figure or *one* finding; nothing answers "how much is in here, is the crawl working, what broke".

**Scope, decided with the owner:** the corpus and the operations only. Nothing about visitors — no search-term logging, no share counters, no client error beacon. Those would each need a write surface (which `5.8` refuses) and a retained record of what a reader typed, and a product whose roster note says *we do not track personal activity* should not start with its own readers. The dashboard answers from what the server already knows about itself.

## What it shows

- **The corpus**: figures, utterances, attestations, clusters, findings — counts, plus the distribution of utterances over venue and over year, and how many carry no date at all.
- **The crawl**: per source module, when it last ran, what it fetched, what came from cache, what failed and why. A module that has **never** run reads as never-run, not as zero — the difference is the whole point of looking.
- **Server-side failures**: the reasons a run recorded, which are already produced by acquisition and the ingestion pipeline and today are thrown away when the scheduled handler returns.

## Two routes, split by what the data actually is

- `GET /api/v1/status` — **public**. Corpus counts and distributions. Every number in it is already derivable from the public corpus API by walking it, so gating it would be theatre.
- `GET /api/v1/operations` — **credentialled**. Runs and failure reasons. Failure text names internals, so this half is not public.

## Auth

A static page cannot hold a secret, so the credential is supplied by whoever is looking: a bearer token compared against a Worker secret, kept in the browser. Unset secret means the route answers "not configured" rather than answering openly — it fails closed and says which.

The alternative worth recording is **Cloudflare Access** in front of the route: it runs the login itself and sets a long-lived HttpOnly cookie, which is the shape the owner asked about. It is not implemented here, because an Access-aware branch has to trust a forwarded identity header, and a branch that trusts a header is a privilege escalation the moment the route is not actually behind Access — and there is no account here to exercise it against (#27). It goes in `DESIGN.md` as the deployment alternative, unexercised and marked so.

## Where it lives

Its own app under `src/dashboard/`, published to GitHub Pages, separate from the product site — the site is a public Hebrew reading surface and this is an English operator tool. The barrier rules gain a third party so the dashboard cannot reach into the backend either.

## Requirements

A new section in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` rather than a second spec file. The harness resolves exactly one `SPEC_PATH` and one requirements root, and the coverage bijection is one leaf ↔ one case across all kinds — a second spec would mean a second gate, a second registry and a second set of runners for requirements about the same product. Section 8, new ids, existing kinds.

Blocked on nothing: it is built and proven against the same fake world as everything else, and lights up with real numbers when #27 lands.

## 6. The site

RTL-first, Hebrew-primary, with the same layout mirrored for LTR content. Each leaf's
expected result is the committed screenshot below it: approving the image is approving the
page. The design system these render is the warm-editorial direction the owner approved on
the design canvas.

- `6.1` The home page leads with the search, then the most recent surfaced inconsistencies, then the tracked figures.
<!-- gallery:6.1 -->

![6.1 — The home page leads with the search, then the most recent surfaced inconsistencies, then the tracked figures.](screen/cases/home.6.1.png)

<!-- /gallery:6.1 -->

- `6.2` A figure page shows the profile, the counts, the named subjects, and the utterance timeline with flagged utterances marked.
<!-- gallery:6.2 -->

![6.2 — A figure page shows the profile, the counts, the named subjects, and the utterance timeline with flagged utterances marked.](screen/cases/figure.6.2.png)

<!-- /gallery:6.2 -->

- `6.3` An utterance page shows what was said, when — to the precision the source established — where, and every document that reported it.
<!-- gallery:6.3 -->

![6.3 — An utterance page shows what was said, when — to the precision the source established — where, and every document that reported it.](screen/cases/utterance.6.3.png)

<!-- /gallery:6.3 -->

- `6.4` A trend-change page shows the two utterances either side of it, separated by the «אבל» mark, with the interval and the rationale.

cat >> dev/requirements/requirements.md <<'EOF'

## 8. The operator dashboard

A separate app for whoever runs this, published apart from the public site: what the corpus
holds, and what the crawl last did. It answers from what the server already knows about
itself — no visitor is counted, no query is retained, and nothing here required a write
surface. Its rendered states are committed screenshots, the same contract as § 6.

- `8.1` `GET /api/v1/status` returns the corpus totals — figures, utterances, attestations, clusters and live findings — and needs no credential.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  Public on purpose. Every number in it can already be arrived at by walking the public
  corpus API, so a credential here would protect nothing and would only stop a researcher
  citing the size of the thing they are citing.
  </details>

- `8.2` `GET /api/v1/status` reports how utterances distribute over venue and over year, counting the undated as their own bucket rather than dropping them.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  A corpus reaching back decades has utterances a source never dated, and `1.3` exists so
  that stays unknown rather than becoming a guess. A distribution that silently omits them
  reports a smaller corpus than there is; one that files them under a year invents the fact
  `1.3` refused to invent.
  </details>

- `8.3` `GET /api/v1/operations` refuses a request carrying no credential, and answers one carrying the configured token.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The operations half reports failure reasons, which name internals. The credential is a
  bearer token compared against a Worker secret, because a static page cannot hold a secret
  and the person looking can.
  </details>

- `8.4` `GET /api/v1/operations` refuses when no credential is configured, rather than answering openly.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The dangerous default. An unset secret must fail closed and say that it is unconfigured —
  a route that opens when its guard is missing is a route with no guard.
  </details>

- `8.5` `GET /api/v1/operations` reports each run's outcome per source module — what it fetched, what it took from cache, and every failure with its reason.

- `8.6` A source module that has never run is reported as never having run, and is never reported as having run and found nothing.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  The distinction the dashboard exists for. A module whose parser broke on the first
  document and a module nobody has wired up both show zero utterances, and only one of them
  is a problem. Unknown is a state of its own here as everywhere else in this corpus.
  </details>

- `8.7` The dashboard shows the corpus totals, both distributions, and the state of every source module on one screen.

- `8.8` The dashboard asks for a token when operations refuses it, and keeps showing the corpus numbers it can read without one.
  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

  Half the page needs no credential. A dashboard that renders an error page because its
  privileged half was refused throws away the half that answered.
  </details>

- `8.9` The dashboard says when it last read the server, and reports a source module's failures against that module rather than in one undifferentiated list.
EOF

-- What the scheduled pass did, per source module, kept rather than discarded.
--
-- Acquisition and the ingestion chain already produce this: counts fetched and taken from
-- cache, and a reason per item that failed. Until now the handler returned and all of it
-- went out of scope, so the only way to know whether the crawl was working was to watch a
-- log stream nobody watches.
--
-- One row per module per pass, not one per pass: modules run on their own clocks, and the
-- question is always about a module — this one has not run since Tuesday — never about
-- the pass as a whole.
CREATE TABLE runs (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- ULID, minted once
  source_module TEXT NOT NULL,
  started_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  finished_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  -- What the pass moved. Zero here is a real zero: the module ran and found nothing new.
  -- A module that has never run has no row at all, which is what keeps never-run and
  -- found-nothing distinguishable (8.6) — absence is the encoding of unknown.
  fetched       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cached        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  utterances    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unattributed  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  -- The reasons, as a JSON array of {key, reason}. Held as one blob rather than a table:
  -- nothing joins on a failure, they are read as a list beside the run they belong to,
  -- and a run with four hundred of them should still be one row to fetch.
  failures      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'
);

-- Every read is "the latest run for each module", so the index is the query.
CREATE INDEX runs_by_module ON runs (source_module, started_at DESC);
EOF

prefix of the real token, which is what a compare that stops early lets through.

A module that has never run has no row, and the view is driven by the registry

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-0/bundled-skills/2.1.241/1d327321ab994dd1b8f4b3a32dc806f7/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

content.content:
# Choosing a form

Decide this **before** color. The data's job picks the form — and sometimes the
right form is not a chart.

## Is it even a chart?

| The data is… | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| A single current value (+ maybe a trend) | **Stat tile** (value + delta + sparkline) | A one-bar bar chart |
| A handful of headline numbers | **KPI row** of stat tiles | A grouped bar chart |
| The one number a dashboard leads with | **Hero figure** (≥48px, sans) | — |
| A single ratio against a limit | **Meter** (same-ramp track) | A pie of 2 slices |
| More than ~7 classes that all carry meaning | A **table** (or table + chart) | More colors |

If a chart *is* right, pick the type by the job:

## The job → the type

| Job (what the reader must do) | Default form | Color job |
|---|---|---|
| Compare magnitude, low → high | bar / column; **heatmap** for a grid | sequential (one hue) |
| Trend over time | line; area for a single series | sequential or 1 categorical |
| Tell distinct series apart | grouped/stacked bar, multi-line | **categorical** |
| One series is the point, rest are context | **emphasis** (highlight one, gray the rest) | 1 hue + gray |
| Above/below a baseline; Δ to target | diverging bar, or line vs baseline | diverging |
| Part-to-whole | **stacked bar** (go horizontal for many / long-named categories) | categorical |
| Ordered-scale share (Likert, sentiment, agree↔disagree) | **diverging stacked bar**, centered on neutral | diverging |
| Before → after per item | dumbbell | 1 hue, 2 shades |

## The rules behind the table

- **Sequential is the safe default.** One hue, more-is-darker. It stays legible and
  consistent and is hard to misread. Reach for it unless the data's job is
  specifically *identity* or *polarity*.
- **Categorical is for when the series ARE the subject** — and it has a real cost:
  it can bury the one data point that actually matters. If the story is "this one
  went up," that's **emphasis**, not categorical.
- **Emphasis** = the most underused form. One series in the accent hue, the rest in
  the de-emphasis gray. Often the honest answer to "make this chart clearer."
- **Texture is an opt-in expression, not a default form.** It earns its place only
  for accessibility (full CVD), print/export, and `forced-colors`. Never decorative.
  → see `marks-and-anatomy.md`.

## Series-count ladder (categorical)

| Series | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | color alone is comfortable for everyone; direct-label |
| 4 | adjacent forms (stacks, bars, lines) stay gate-safe, but direct labels become mandatory — yellow and orange now share the screen; all-pairs forms (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small multiples) cap at **three** — fold to "Other" or facet rather than seat a 4th |
| 5–6 | soft cap; legend or small multiples |
| 7–8 | token ceiling; past it, fold the tail into "Other," facet into small multiples, or use composite encoding (hue × shape) |

Never solve "too many series" by generating more hues. A generated 9th hue is
indistinguishable from an existing one under CVD and breaks every check.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('dev/requirements/screen/harness.ts'); s = p.read_text()

old = """const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));
const DIST = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'src/frontend/dist');"""
new = """const REPO_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

old_origin = """/** An https origin: geolocation and other capabilities only exist on a secure one, and
 *  routes are fulfilled before any connection, so no certificate is involved. */
export const SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://hitbut.test';"""
new_origin = """/** An https origin: geolocation and other capabilities only exist on a secure one, and
 *  routes are fulfilled before any connection, so no certificate is involved. */
export const SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://hitbut.test';

/**
 * One built app, and the origin it is served from. Two of them, because the product site
 * and the operator console are separate artifacts that ship to different hosts — giving
 * them one origin here would let a case pass on a link between them that cannot exist.
 */
export type App = { origin: string; dist: string; config: string };

export const SITE: App = {
  origin: SITE_ORIGIN,
  dist: path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'src/frontend/dist'),
  config: path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'src/frontend/vite.config.ts'),
};

export const DASHBOARD: App = {
  origin: 'https://operator.hitbut.test',
  dist: path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'src/dashboard/dist'),
  config: path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'src/dashboard/vite.config.ts'),
};"""
assert old_origin in s
s = s.replace(old_origin, new_origin, 1)

old_ctx = """export async function newContext(
  browser: Browser,
  api: (pathAndQuery: string) => Promise<{ status: number; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string }>,
  viewport: Viewport,
): Promise<BrowserContext> {"""
new_ctx = """export async function newContext(
  browser: Browser,
  api: (pathAndQuery: string) => Promise<{ status: number; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string }>,
  viewport: Viewport,
  app: App = SITE,
): Promise<BrowserContext> {"""
assert old_ctx in s
s = s.replace(old_ctx, new_ctx, 1)

old_route = """    if (url.origin !== SITE_ORIGIN) return route.abort();"""
new_route = """    if (url.origin !== app.origin) return route.abort();"""
assert old_route in s
s = s.replace(old_route, new_route, 1)

old_asset = """    const asset = path.join(DIST, url.pathname);
    const file = existsSync(asset) && path.extname(asset) ? asset : path.join(DIST, 'index.html');"""
new_asset = """    const asset = path.join(app.dist, url.pathname);
    const file = existsSync(asset) && path.extname(asset) ? asset : path.join(app.dist, 'index.html');"""
assert old_asset in s
s = s.replace(old_asset, new_asset, 1)
p.write_text(s)
print('harness parameterised')
PY

input.command:
cat > .github/workflows/dashboard.yml <<'EOF'
# The operator dashboard on GitHub Pages: a static console, published apart from the
# product site, which ships to Cloudflare Pages from `product.yml`.
#
# Two things it is not. It is not a build of the corpus — every number it shows it reads
# live from the Worker at view time, so a stale publish still shows fresh data. And it
# holds no credential: the API origin below is public, and the operations half asks
# whoever is looking for a token, which lives in their browser and never in this artifact.
name: dashboard

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'src/dashboard/**'
      - 'src/shared/**'
      - '.github/workflows/dashboard.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Pages takes one deployment at a time. A queued run supersedes an older queued one, but
# never cancels one already publishing — a half-written site is worse than an old one.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  publish:
    name: publish the console
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      # Baked in at build time, because the console is static and has no server to ask.
      # Absent, the page says it has no API origin rather than silently showing nothing.
      - name: Build
        env:
          VITE_API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
        run: npm run build:dashboard
      # Three different majors on purpose: these are the versions that run on Node 24,
      # read from each action's own action.yml rather than assumed to move together.
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v6
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: src/dashboard/dist
      - id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
EOF

cat > src/dashboard/README.md <<'EOF'
# dashboard

The operator console: what the corpus holds, and what each source module last did. A
static Preact app on GitHub Pages, published by `.github/workflows/dashboard.yml`,
separate from the product site in `../frontend`.

It reads two routes over the same public HTTP API a reader's browser uses. `/status` needs
no credential — every number in it is reachable by walking the corpus API. `/operations`
does, and the token lives in the operator's browser: a static page cannot hold a secret,
so it is supplied by whoever is looking rather than shipped in the bundle.

Nothing here counts a visitor to the site. Its numbers come from what the server already
knows about itself, which is why it needed no write surface — see § 8 of
[the requirements](../../dev/requirements/requirements.md) and the reasoning in
[`DESIGN.md`](../../docs/architecture/DESIGN.md).

`npm run dev:dashboard` runs it; `npm run build:dashboard` builds it. Both take the API
origin from `VITE_API_ORIGIN`.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('docs/architecture/DESIGN.md'); s = p.read_text()
anchor = """## Frontend"""
section = """## The operator console

A second static app, on GitHub Pages rather than Cloudflare Pages, answering the question
the public API cannot: not "what did this person say" but "how much is in here, is the
crawl working, what broke". It reads `/api/v1/status` and `/api/v1/operations`.

**The split between those two routes is by what the data is.** Corpus totals and
distributions are public, because every number in them can already be arrived at by
walking the corpus API — a credential there would protect nothing and would stop a
researcher citing the size of what they cite. Run outcomes are not, because a failure
reason names internals.

**It counts nobody.** No search term is retained, no view is tallied, no client error is
beaconed home. Each of those would need a write surface — which `5.8` refuses — and would
start a record about the people reading a corpus whose own roster says we do not track
personal activity. What the console shows, the server already knew about itself.

**The credential is supplied by whoever is looking.** A static page cannot hold a secret,
so the token is compared against a Worker secret and kept in the operator's browser. An
unset secret closes the route and says so, rather than opening it.

*Alternative — Cloudflare Access in front of the route*: this is the shape worth reaching
for later. Access runs the login itself and leaves a long-lived HttpOnly cookie, so no
token touches JavaScript. Two things stop it being the answer today. Its cookie belongs to
the hostname Access protects and its login is a redirect a `fetch` cannot follow, so the
console would have to move off GitHub Pages onto a Cloudflare hostname. And an
Access-aware branch has to trust a forwarded identity header, which is a privilege
escalation the moment the route is not actually behind Access — so it is not written until
there is an account (#27) to exercise it against. Unbuilt and unexercised, deliberately.

**A module that has never run reads as never-run.** The view is driven by the source
registry rather than by the runs table, so a module with no rows is listed and marked,
never omitted and never shown as a run that found nothing. Absence is how "unknown" is
encoded here, as everywhere else in this corpus.

## Frontend"""
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, section, 1)
p.write_text(s)
PY

input.title: An operator console: what the corpus holds, and what the crawl did
input.head: claude/hitbut-dashboard
input.body:
Nine leaves under a new § 8, written first and watched red before anything implemented them.

## Scope

The corpus and the operations only. No search-term logging, no view counters, no client error beacon — each would need a write surface (`5.8` refuses one) and would start a retained record about the people *reading* a corpus whose own roster note says we do not track personal activity. Everything on the screen, the server already knew about itself.

## Two routes, split by what the data is

- `GET /api/v1/status` — **public**. Every number in it is reachable by walking the corpus API, so a credential would protect nothing and would stop a researcher citing the size of what they cite.
- `GET /api/v1/operations` — **credentialled**. A failure reason names internals.

The credential **fails closed**: an unset secret answers `operations_unconfigured` rather than answering openly, and `8.4` holds the *shipped Worker on the committed config* to that — where `DASHBOARD_TOKEN` genuinely is unset, because a secret is not in a config file. That is the deploy that forgets it, tested as itself.

## What the tests caught

- **`8.3` did not catch a weak comparison.** Perturbing `sameSecret` to accept a prefix left the case green — it tested a longer token and a same-length wrong one, never a strict prefix, which is exactly what a compare that stops at the first difference lets through. The case now covers it, and reddens.
- **The screen lane found a determinism defect in my own page.** The masthead printed the *server's* wall clock, so three goldens drifted 36–64 pixels per run. It now reads this device's clock — which is what "how fresh is the screen in front of me" actually asks — while the server's `readAt` stays on the wire, where staleness is measured against it, because a run's timestamps are the server's. Green twice consecutively after.
- **The ordering gate caught a prose `1.3` at the start of a line** in one of the new `<details>` blocks, and named the file and line. Third time it has paid for itself.
- **The barrier check refused the dashboard README** for pointing at `../frontend` in a sentence. It was right; the sentence says it without the path now.

## The charts

The first pass drew them as SVG with a fixed `viewBox` and both rendered **letterboxed** — bars floating in a gutter at any width a real container has. They are CSS marks now, so they reflow. Length carries magnitude in both, leaving colour one job and one hue. The state chips are the only meaningful colour and each carries its word too; the ok/stale/failing set was run through a palette validator, which rejected my first four-colour set (grey ↔ oxide, ΔE 14.9 — below the normal-vision floor, and they are the two states this page exists to tell apart). **Never-run draws no status colour at all**: it is the absence of a reading, not a fourth state beside the others, and every one of its cells is a dash rather than a zero.

## Requirements: one spec, new section

Not a second file. The harness resolves exactly one `SPEC_PATH` and one requirements root, and the bijection is one leaf ↔ one case across all kinds — a second spec means a second gate, a second registry and a second set of runners, for requirements about the same product. § 8, new ids, existing kinds.

## Your question about a Cloudflare login

Recorded in `DESIGN.md` as the alternative, deliberately unbuilt. Three things worth knowing: the data lives in **our** D1, not in Cloudflare's API, so a Cloudflare token authenticates against the wrong system; even a read-only one is account-scoped, far more authority than showing corpus counts needs; and **Cloudflare Access** *is* the flow you described — it runs the login and leaves a long-lived HttpOnly cookie — but its cookie belongs to the hostname it protects and its login is a redirect a `fetch` cannot follow, so the console would have to move off GitHub Pages onto a Cloudflare hostname. I did not write the Access branch: it must trust a forwarded identity header, which is a privilege escalation the moment the route is not actually behind Access, and there is no account here to exercise it against. I also could not verify Cloudflare's own specifics — the sandbox gateway refuses `api.cloudflare.com` and `developers.cloudflare.com` at CONNECT, a policy denial confirmed in the proxy's own status.

## Verification

`npm test` 65 · `npm run test:server` 16 · `npm run test:screen` 17 (twice) · typecheck clean · `check_the_world.mjs` 0 blocking · `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolving three bindings.

Closes #81

input.title: Turn on GitHub Pages for the operator console (human-only steps)
input.body:
The console and its publish workflow are merged, but nothing can publish until Pages is switched on for this repository. No session can do it — it is a repository setting.

Until this is done, `.github/workflows/dashboard.yml` fails at `configure-pages` on every push that touches `src/dashboard/`. That is the only symptom; nothing else is affected.

- [ ] **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions.** Not "Deploy from a branch" — the workflow uploads an artifact and deploys it, and a branch source ignores the workflow entirely. Off: the publish job fails and there is no console.
- [ ] **Settings → Environments → `github-pages`.** Created on the first successful deploy; nothing to do unless you want to restrict which branches may publish, in which case allow `main` only. Off: any branch that could run the workflow could publish over the console.
- [ ] **Settings → Variables → Actions → `API_ORIGIN`.** The Worker's public origin, e.g. `https://hitbut-api.<subdomain>.workers.dev`. This is the same variable the deploy job already reads, so it may already exist. Off: the console builds and loads, and says it has no API origin instead of showing numbers — it does not fail silently.

**Closing condition:** the workflow's run is green, `https://<owner>.github.io/hitbut/` loads the console, the corpus tiles show real numbers, and the sources section asks for a token.

The token itself is separate and is Cloudflare's side: `wrangler secret put DASHBOARD_TOKEN`, tracked with the rest of provisioning in #27. Until it is set, the console correctly shows the corpus half and reports the operations half as unconfigured.

Refs #81, #27

people — the barrier rules gain a third party so neither can reach into the

both charts rendered letterboxed inside it, floating in a gutter at any width a
container actually has. Length carries magnitude in both, which leaves colour one
job and one hue; the state chips are the only colour that means anything, and
each carries its word too. Never-run draws no status colour at all: it is the
absence of a reading rather than a fourth state beside the others.

a determinism defect on its first run: the masthead was printing the *server's*
wall clock, which moved every run. It now reads this device's clock, which is
what "how fresh is the screen in front of me" actually asks; the server's own
readAt stays on the wire, where staleness is measured against it, because a
run's timestamps are the server's. Green twice consecutively after the fix.

{"id":32639373505,"name":"product","display_title":"product","workflow_id":339572729,"run_number":46,"run_attempt":1,"event":"workflow_dispatch","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"claude/hitbut-dashboard","head_sha":"471379e33db911bf47ba464ddb3969d96a94a75e","head_commit":{"message":"Give the operator a console, and a second app to put it in

One screen: the corpus totals, where and when its utterances were said, and what
each source module last did. Its own app on its own origin, because the public
site and an internal console ship to different hosts and answer to different
people — the barrier rules gain a third party so neither can reach into the
other.

The charts are CSS rather than SVG. The first pass used a fixed viewBox and
both charts rendered letterboxed inside it, floating in a gutter at any width a
container actually has. Length carries magnitude in both, which leaves colour one
job and one hue; the state chips are the only colour that means anything, and
each carries its word too. Never-run draws no status colour at all: it is the
absence of a reading rather than a fourth state beside the others.

The screen lane learned about a second app rather than a second lane, and found
a determinism defect on its first run: the masthead was printing the *server's*
wall clock, which moved every run. It now reads this device's clock, which is
what "how fresh is the screen in front of me" actually asks; the server's own
readAt stays on the wire, where staleness is measured against it, because a
run's timestamps are the server's. Green twice consecutively after the fix.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.
content.activeForm: Wiring deploy and filing the provisioning issue

One screen: the corpus totals, where and when its utterances were said, and what
each source module last did. Its own app on its own origin, because the public
site and an internal console ship to different hosts and answer to different
people — the barrier rules gain a third party so neither can reach into the
other.

The charts are CSS rather than SVG. The first pass used a fixed viewBox and
both charts rendered letterboxed inside it, floating in a gutter at any width a
container actually has. Length carries magnitude in both, which leaves colour one
job and one hue; the state chips are the only colour that means anything, and
each carries its word too. Never-run draws no status colour at all: it is the
absence of a reading rather than a fourth state beside the others.

The screen lane learned about a second app rather than a second lane, and found
a determinism defect on its first run: the masthead was printing the *server's*
wall clock, which moved every run. It now reads this device's clock, which is
what "how fresh is the screen in front of me" actually asks; the server's own
readAt stays on the wire, where staleness is measured against it, because a
run's timestamps are the server's. Green twice consecutively after the fix.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

input.commit_title: An operator console: what the corpus holds, and what the crawl did (#85)
input.commit_message:
Nine leaves under a new section 8, written first and watched red. Two routes
split by what the data is: status public, operations credentialled and failing
closed on an unset secret. A second static app on its own origin, with the
barrier rules gaining a third party.

Verified by CI on 471379e: 65 default-lane, 16 server on real workerd, 17 screen
goldens, typecheck and the wrangler dry-run — the three new goldens render
byte-identically on a runner, which is what the determinism fix in the last
commit was for.

Closes #81

input.commit_title: An operator console: what the corpus holds, and what the crawl did (#85)
input.commit_message:
Nine leaves under a new section 8, written first and watched red. Two routes
split by what the data is: status public, operations credentialled and failing
closed on an unset secret. A second static app on its own origin, with the
barrier rules gaining a third party. Nothing counts a visitor.

Verified by CI on 6ecdf56, after merging main: 94 default-lane, 16 server on
real workerd, 17 screen goldens, typecheck and the wrangler dry-run. The three
new goldens render byte-identically on a runner, which is what the determinism
fix was for — the masthead had been printing the server's wall clock.

Closes #81
